column5: You are not my Father.
column6: 你不是我的父亲。

column5: Do you say this to inform us, or to console {i}yourself{/i}?
column6: 你说这话，是为了告知我们，还是为了安慰{i}你自己{/i}？

column5: Huh...?
This question was self explanatory.
column6: 这个问题不言自明。

column5: It's just — I should be mad at you. Furious.\nYou defile the memory and likeness of my Father.
column6: 只是——我本该对你发火。暴怒。\n你在玷污我父亲的记忆与形象。

column5: Do we...?\nIt seems that \"Salus\" was an honorable man.\nAre we not carrying out his final wishes?
column6: 我们吗……？\n看来“萨鲁斯”是个可敬的人。\n我们不是在完成他最后的遗愿吗？

column5: What?
column6: 什么？

column5: The freedom of Alestia. The destruction of The Triumvirate.\nWhen you look at it that way, it seems as if we defile nothing
column6: 阿拉斯提亚的自由。三人执政团的覆灭。\n这么一看，我们似乎什么也没有玷污

column5: I... I don't know.
column6: 我……我不知道。

column5: What are you wishing to know?
column6: 你想知道什么？

column5: I want to know how I should feel right now!\nThis is just so bizarre — I have no idea what to do.\nBack in Valinorth, things were so simple, and easy.
column6: 我想知道我现在该有什么感觉！\n这太离奇了——我完全不知道该怎么办。\n在瓦利诺斯的时候，一切都那么简单、轻松。

column5: Why must you do anything?\nYou could mull over this development for years, you know.\nAt the end of the day, you should do something more useful.
column6: 你为什么非得做什么呢？\n你知道，你大可把这件事琢磨上好几年。\n说到底，你应该去做些更有用的事。

column5: Like what?
column6: 比如什么？

column5: This is not for us to decide.\nBut have no worries, we will take care of this body.\nAnd using it, we will do everything we can to honor your Father.
column6: 这不是我们能决定的。\n但别担心，我们会照看好这具身体。\n并利用它，竭尽所能地荣耀你的父亲。

column5: Thank you...\nI'll let you know if I think of anything.\nThis might take a while for me to understand.
column6: 谢谢……\n如果我想到了什么，会告诉你的。\n我可能需要一段时间才能理解这件事。

column5: Very well, but please remember this.\nLack of understanding is not a fault. In fact, it can be a strength.\nYou flourished even though you did not know the truth of the spirits.
column6: 很好，但请记住这一点。\n不理解并不是过错。事实上，它也可以是一种力量。\n即便你不知道灵的真相，你依然茁壮成长。

column5: You're right...\nI think I need some time alone.\nI'll be down in the crew quarters, Howl.
column6: 你说得对……\n我想我需要一个人静一静。\n我会待在下面的船员舱，豪尔。

column5: I need to thank you again, Pommy.\nYour support means a lot to me. It truly does.\nSome of the rebels have started to side with Howl.
column6: 我得再次感谢你，波米。\n你的支持对我意义重大。真的。\n有些反抗军成员已经开始站到豪尔那边了。

column5: A pretty dumb decision, if you ask me.\nI know what they're thinking — that {i}you're{/i} responsible.\nBut that's impossible. Nobody could've seen what was coming.
column6: 要我说，这决定可真够蠢的。\n我知道他们在想什么——觉得{i}你{/i}该负责。\n但那不可能。没人能预见会发生什么。

column5: Yeah, we were played. Caught off guard.\nI know it won't happen again, though. Things are different.\nIt's almost like our belief in the spirit realm was holding us back.
column6: 是啊，我们被算计了。措手不及。\n不过我知道这种事不会再发生了。情况不一样了。\n就好像我们对灵界的信仰一直在拖我们的后腿。

column5: Do you think the people will even believe us, though?\nI mean, do {i}you{/i} even believe the truth we've been told?
column6: 可你觉得民众会相信我们吗？\n我是说，{i}你{/i}自己相信我们听到的真相吗？

column5: I don't really have a choice, Damek.\nYour speech gave us proof. It was undeniable.\nI'd advise doing the same thing to every other Alestian.
column6: 我其实没有选择，达梅克。\n你的演讲给了我们证据。无可辩驳。\n我建议对每一个阿拉斯提亚人都这么做。

column5: Even if it takes years, you can do it.\nI'll even help you if you need assistance.\nNobody said that things would be easy after the war.
column6: 就算要花上数年，你也能做到。\n如果你需要帮忙，我甚至会帮你。\n没人说过战后一切会轻松。

column5: You're right, and thanks for that offer. \nI'm pretty sure I'll take you up on it — since this is a tall order.\nBut I know that almost {i}anything{/i} is possible, if we all band together.
column6: 你说得对，谢谢你的提议。\n我很确定我会接受——毕竟这是件难办的差事。\n但我知道，只要我们团结一心，几乎{i}任何事{/i}都可能。

column5: Of course. So for now, we need to fix the discord in our ranks.\nI'll talk with the rebels that are siding with Howl. They need to stop.\nThere {i}are{/i} no sides in this. We all fight for the same cause.
column6: 当然。所以眼下，我们得解决队伍内部的分歧。\n我会去和那些支持豪尔的反抗军成员谈谈。他们必须停下。\n这件事{i}没有{/i}派系之分。我们都在为同一个目标而战。

column5: And if they put their differences aside?\nWell, Damek? We'll win this thing for sure.
column6: 要是他们能放下分歧呢？\n怎么样，达梅克？那我们肯定能赢下这场仗。

column5: Hey Pro, can I talk to you for a second?
column6: 嘿，普洛，我能跟你聊两句吗？

column5: Of course! What's up?
column6: 当然！怎么了？

column5: I can't say in front of everybody else.\nI need to talk to you alone. In {i}secret{/i}.
column6: 我不能当着大家的面说。\n我需要单独跟你谈。{i}秘密{/i}地谈。

column5: Oh, is it about {i}that{/i}?
column6: 哦，是关于{i}那件事{/i}吗？

column5: Pro. Not in front of anybody else.\nFollow me over here, and talk quietly.
column6: 普洛。别当着别人的面。\n跟我到这边来，小声说。

column5: Right, right. Sorry.\nWell then, what's up?
column6: 好，好。抱歉。\n那么，怎么了？

column5: So, what's it like to be a Seer...?\nWhat kind of stuff are you starting to see?\nDoes it hurt your head? Are you enjoying it...?
column6: 那么，当先知是什么感觉……？\n你开始看到什么样的东西了？\n会头疼吗？你享受这种感觉吗……？

column5: It gives me great pleasure to see the future.\nBut right now, it's just little things. Indecipherable.\nPerhaps as we process this, things will get more clear.
column6: 能预见未来让我非常愉悦。\n但眼下，只是些琐碎的东西。难以解读。\n也许随着我们慢慢消化，一切会变得更清晰。

column5: I see loss in the future. Loss, and tragedy.\nBut for which side of this battle, I cannot say.\nIt seems to be a \"gut feeling\", at the moment.
column6: 我在未来看到了失去。失去，还有悲剧。\n但属于这场战斗的哪一方，我说不上来。\n目前，这似乎只是一种“直觉”。

column5: Yeah, it's the same for me. Brief flashes.\nBut I see a coliseum, and a big struggle.\nI think you'll all be fighting during your visit.
column6: 是啊，我也是这样。短暂的闪现。\n但我看到了一座竞技场，还有一场激烈的厮杀。\n我想你们这次到访期间都会参战。

column5: Fighting...? That's no fun.\nHopefully your powers get better over time.\nImagine how strong you'd be in those battles...!
column6: 参战……？那可不好玩。\n希望你的力量能随着时间变强。\n想象一下你在那些战斗里会有多强……！

column5: Able to see every move before the enemy even makes it.\nWith that power, we'd never have to worry about tragedy or loss.\nI can tell you're going to be one of the best assets in this war.
column6: 能在敌人出手之前就看穿每一个动作。\n有了那种力量，我们就永远不必担心悲剧和失去。\n我敢说你会成为这场战争中最宝贵的战力之一。

column5: Why thank you. That means a lot.\nI'm happy to serve The Rebellion in any way I can.\nWhat they did back in those tunnels was inexcusable.
column6: 哎呀，谢谢你。这对我意义重大。\n我很乐意尽我所能为反抗军效力。\n他们在那些隧道里的所作所为不可饶恕。

column5: Yeah. I'd say we show them the same treatment.\nWe'll fight for a future that all of you can enjoy.\nEven if we can't join that future ourselves.
column6: 是啊。要我说，我们也该让他们尝尝同样的滋味。\n我们会为你们所有人都能享受的未来而战。\n哪怕我们自己无法置身于那个未来。

column5: That's certainly a pessimistic view, Ignace.\nThere might be a way to save our minds, you know.\nThis Rebellion has proved that {i}anything{/i} is possible.
column6: 这看法可真是悲观，伊格纳斯。\n你知道，也许有办法拯救我们的心智。\n这场反抗已经证明了{i}一切{/i}皆有可能。

column5: Yeah, you're right.\nWe'll make it through this.
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n我们会挺过去的。

column5: So what's it like...?\nYou know, being a vessel.
column6: 那么那是什么感觉……？\n你知道的，当一具容器。

column5: It is not much different than when we were alive.\nThere are simply voices in our head. Lots of them.\nThe Monarchy guides our every move. It is hard to explain.
column6: 和我们活着的时候没太大区别。\n只是脑子里多了些声音。很多声音。\n王室指引着我们的每一个举动。很难解释清楚。

column5: They are fueled by the rage of their imprisonment.\nEverything inside of us tells us to fight, and to kill.\nWhen the time comes, we will fight for this world.
column6: 他们被囚禁的怒火驱动着。\n我们内在的一切都在叫嚣着战斗、杀戮。\n到时候，我们会为这个世界而战。

column5: The wounds on our bodies hurt us at first.\nBut like white noise, we have phased it out.\nIt only flares up every few minutes, now.
column6: 我们身上的伤口起初很疼。\n但就像白噪音一样，我们已将它屏蔽。\n现在只是每隔几分钟发作一次。

column5: And how bad is it...?
column6: 那有多严重……？

column5: We feel every wound as if freshly inflicted.\nIt is almost like we exist on the edge of life and death.\nOur body is unable to fully commit to either side of the spectrum.
column6: 我们感受每一道伤口，仿佛新添的一般。\n几乎就像我们存在于生与死的边缘。\n我们的身体无法完全归属于任何一端。

column5: That sounds horrible...
column6: 听起来太可怕了……

column5: Horrible, yes. But also necessary.\nWith our aid, The Triumvirate shall fall.\nJustice will finally be given to The Monarchy.
column6: 是的，可怕。但也必要。\n有我们的相助，三人执政团必将覆灭。\n正义终将归于王室。

column5: When we can deliver that justice, the pain is worth it.\nWe embrace this as a gift, and will honor The Monarch.\nWithout their choice, we would not be alive to fight.
column6: 当我们能亲手带来那份正义时，这痛苦就值得了。\n我们将此视为恩赐，并会荣耀君主。\n若非君主的选择，我们不会活着战斗。

column5: I just wish there was a way to make the pain go away.\nYou know, after this war, you're still going to suffer.
column6: 我只希望能有办法让痛苦消失。\n你知道的，这场战争之后，你依然会受苦。

column5: We are not the only ones who will continue to suffer.\nThe wounds endured during this war can also be emotional.\nScars will haunt {i}all{/i} of your forces. We are not the only ones.
column6: 会继续受苦的不止我们。\n这场战争留下的创伤也可以是情感上的。\n伤疤会萦绕在你们{i}所有{/i}人的心头。不止我们。

column5: Right...
column6: 是啊……

column6: 那么那是什么感觉……？\n你知道的，当一具容器。

column5: Right...
column6: 是啊……

column5: So we might have to fight Ulric?\nThat's pretty scary to think about, Pro.
column6: 所以我们可能得和乌尔里克交手？\n想想就挺可怕的，普洛。

column5: Only if [firstname] sides with Draycu, Valessa.\nThere's still a pretty good chance that won't happen.\nI wonder who Draycu will elect as his champion, though.
column6: 只有在[firstname]站到德雷库那边的情况下，瓦莱莎。\n那件事不发生的可能性还挺大的。\n不过，我很好奇德雷库会选谁当他的斗士。

column5: Well his army is supposed to be incredibly powerful.\nHe must get to hand pick the strongest Alarinthians.\nI'm sure Ulric can handle it, though. At least, I hope.
column6: 他的军队据说强大得惊人。\n他肯定能亲手挑选最强的阿拉林西亚人。\n不过我相信乌尔里克能应付。至少，我希望如此。

column5: Well, Draycu doesn't like to waste his men, remember?\nIt's possible he'll elect an outsider, meaning one of {i}us{/i}.\nVivien is like an insect to him — super easy to crush.
column6: 这个嘛，德雷库不喜欢浪费自己的手下，记得吗？\n他有可能选一个外人，也就是{i}我们{/i}中的一员。\n薇薇安对他来说就像只虫子——轻易就能捏碎。

column5: So we'll be fighting each other in the end...?\nIsn't this supposed to be a fight to the death?
column6: 所以到最后，我们要自相残杀……？\n这难道不该是场生死决斗吗？

column5: Exciting, isn't it?
column6: 很刺激，不是吗？

column5: No, it's not! That means one of us will die!
column6: 不，才不是！那意味着我们中会有人死去！

column5: Not exactly...
column6: 也不尽然……

column5: Huh?
column6: 嗯？

column5: The match ends if the champion, {i}or{/i} the leader falls.\nIt'd be possible to end this with Vivien or Draycu's death.\nThe Champion is just there to spice things up, I guess.
column6: 只要斗士{i}或{/i}领袖倒下，比试就结束了。\n所以也可能以薇薇安或德雷库的死来收场。\n我猜，斗士的存在只是为了让场面更刺激。

column5: If it were just the two leaders, they'd only fight each other.\nHaving two champions ensures the fight constantly changes pace.\nIt makes things sound more interesting, at least. You need {i}strategy{/i}.
column6: 如果只有两位领袖，他们就只会互相厮杀。\n有两名斗士在，战斗的节奏才能不断变化。\n至少这样听起来更有意思。你需要{i}策略{/i}。

column5: Watching two leaders in an unending deadlock would be boring.\nThe Champions and a small army of men really shake it up.\nIt makes sure the leaders are at the top of their game, too.
column6: 看着两位领袖陷入没完没了的僵局会很无聊。\n斗士们和一小队士兵确实能让局面翻天覆地。\n这也能确保领袖们发挥出最佳状态。

column5: They have to watch {i}every{/i} direction; and constantly be ready.\nIt serves to show us how strong they {i}truly{/i} are. It's crazy.\nDraycu is undefeated, but Ulric might just stand a chance.
column6: 他们得提防{i}每一个{/i}方向，还得时刻保持戒备。\n这也正好向人们展示他们{i}究竟{/i}有多强。太疯狂了。\n德雷库从未败过，但乌尔里克或许还真有一拼之力。

column5: I think you're kind of missing my point, Pro...
column6: 我觉得你有点没抓住我的重点，普洛……

column5: Really?
column6: 是吗？

column5: I don't think of Vivien and Draycu as expendable.\nAt the end of the day, one of us will die no matter what.\nEven if it's one of them, it's still something I'd like to avoid.
column6: 我不觉得薇薇安和德雷库是可以牺牲的。\n说到底，无论如何我们中都会有人死去。\n就算死的是他们中的一个，我也还是想尽量避免。

column5: Then it sounds like you side with Vivien, then.\nDraycu's death would be the final death in the coliseum.\nThere'd be no more fights like this under his reign.
column6: 那听起来你是站在薇薇安这边了。\n德雷库的死会是竞技场的最后一场死亡。\n在他的统治下，再也不会有这样的决斗。

column5: I know you're right, but it's not so easy.\nWe have to kill him just because he thinks differently?\nThere's no way to avoid casualties — and I hate that.
column6: 我知道你说得对，但没那么容易。\n就因为他想法不同，我们就得杀了他？\n没办法避免伤亡——我讨厌这一点。

column5: Yeah, but it's not just Alarinthia, Valessa.\nYou could say that about this entire war in general.\nSometimes it's better to look at people as \"means to an end\".
column6: 是啊，但不止是阿拉林西亚，瓦莱莎。\n整场战争都可以这么说。\n有时候，把别人看作“达到目的的手段”会更好。

column5: I could never do that...
column6: 我永远做不到……

column5: A lot of people feel the same way, trust me.\nBut that's probably why The Triumvirate is in charge.\nWe need to start looking at things differently if we want to win.
column6: 很多人都有同感，相信我。\n但也许正因为如此，掌权的是三人执政团。\n如果我们想赢，就得开始换个角度看问题。

column5: If we have to compromise ourselves, then is it truly winning...?\nI don't know, Pro. I think I need a little bit of time to myself.
column6: 如果我们必须违背自己的本心，那还算是真正的胜利吗……？\n我不知道，普洛。我想我需要一点独处的时间。

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: I don't want to watch Ulric fight in the coliseum...\nIf [firstname] sides with Draycu, then he could die.
column6: 我不想看乌尔里克在竞技场里战斗……\n如果[firstname]站到德雷库那边，他可能会死。

column5: But he's prepared to die for his beliefs, Fortaime.\nThere isn't a better way to go. A true, noble end.
column6: 但他已准备好为信念赴死，福泰姆。\n没有比这更好的死法了。真正高尚的结局。

column5: Honestly, I'd prefer if his life had no end at all.\nI have a feeling this choice will end up dividing us.\nI don't want to fight against Ulric, or watch him die.
column6: 说实话，我倒宁愿他的生命根本没有终点。\n我有种预感，这个选择最终会让我们分裂。\n我不想与乌尔里克为敌，也不想看他死去。

column5: It's all about respecting his wishes, Fortaime.\nIf he puts his life on the line for Alarinthia, we can't deny that.\nYou'd do the same for Valinorth. In fact, you already are.
column6: 关键在于尊重他的意愿，福泰姆。\n如果他愿为阿拉林西亚冒生命危险，我们无法否定。\n你也会为瓦利诺斯这么做。事实上，你已经在这么做了。

column5: Really...?
column6: 真的吗……？

column5: This war is just battle after battle, Fortaime.\nYou put your life on the line back at the Rebel HQ.\nThat means you were ready to die for your beliefs.
column6: 这场战争就是一场接一场的战斗，福泰姆。\n你在反抗军总部时就冒过生命危险。\n那意味着你早已准备好为信念而死。

column5: I guess you're right, when you put it that way.
column6: 这么说的话，你大概是对的。

column5: So Ulric isn't just fighting for Alarinthia.\nRemember that our army gets a boost out of this.\nAt the end of the way, it benefits all of Alestia.
column6: 所以乌尔里克不只是在为阿拉林西亚而战。\n记住，我们的军队也会因此得到增强。\n说到底，这对整个阿拉斯提亚都有好处。

column5: But what if the person we side with loses...?
column6: 但要是我们支持的人输了呢……？

column5: That's what makes things difficult, Fortaime.\nVivien is the right choice, in my opinion, but not the correct one.\nThe correct choice is Draycu. He's won every battle, and has a huge army.
column6: 这才让事情变得棘手，福泰姆。\n在我看来，薇薇安是正确的选择，却不是明智的选择。\n明智的选择是德雷库。他每战必胜，还拥有一支庞大的军队。

column5: This is pretty complicated...\nSo far, every choice was concrete.\nThere was no room to choose, and then lose.
column6: 这相当复杂……\n到目前为止，每个选择都很明确。\n没有可能选了之后还会输。

column5: Alarinthia is different than everything we know.\nI guess it makes sense that things would change once we arrived.\n[firstname] has a tough choice to make. It's a gamble, at best.
column6: 阿拉林西亚和我们所知的一切都不同。\n我们一到，事情就发生变化，也说得通。\n[firstname]要做一个艰难的选择。往好里说，这也是一场赌博。

column5: It shouldn't have to be that way, though...\nThe future of a nation, and our world, is a gamble...?\nThat's bad news. Vivien has the right idea here, for sure.
column6: 可本不该如此……\n一个国家、乃至我们整个世界的未来，竟是一场赌博……？\n这可不是好消息。在这一点上，薇薇安的想法绝对是对的。

column5: You mean abolishing coliseum battles?
column6: 你是说废除竞技场决斗？

column5: Yeah. Things should be just like the rest of Alestia.\nIf they were, then we wouldn't even be in this situation.
column6: 对。这里本该和阿拉斯提亚其他地方一样。\n如果真是那样，我们根本不会落到这步田地。

column5: But we shouldn't change something just because we don't like it.\nThat's what The Triumvirate did to this whole world. We can't be like them.\nAlarinthia has been fine since the dawn of time, it can continue to be fine.
column6: 但我们不该仅仅因为不喜欢就去改变一件事。\n三人执政团对整个世界就是这么干的。我们不能像他们一样。\n阿拉林西亚自开天辟地以来一直如此，也可以继续如此。

column5: Besides, Valinorth is the exact same way.\nIndependent, with its own hierarchy, and leadership.
column6: 再说，瓦利诺斯也是完全一样。\n独立自主，有自己的等级制度和领袖。

column5: It was, but I'm going to change that.\nAs the Elder, I want unity with the other nations.\nI think the same would be best for Alarinthia.
column6: 曾经是的，但我要改变这一点。\n身为长老，我希望与其他国家团结一致。\n我觉得阿拉林西亚也最好如此。

column5: The Triumvirate changed this world to suit {i}them{/i}, right?\nThat's not what we're doing. We're liberating it, making it better.\nOur end goal is different, so I don't think we can be compared to them.
column6: 三人执政团为了{i}他们自己{/i}改变了这个世界，对吧？\n我们不是在干那种事。我们是在解放它，让它变得更好。\n我们的最终目标不同，所以我认为我们不能和他们相提并论。

column5: Well, Valessa plans to keep it that way, yeah.\nBut honestly, I want unity with the other nations.\nI think the same would be best for Alarinthia.
column6: 这个嘛，瓦莱莎打算保持原样，没错。\n但说实话，我希望与其他国家团结一致。\n我觉得阿拉林西亚也最好如此。

column5: The Triumvirate changed this world to suit {i}them{/i}, right?\nThat's not what we're doing. We're liberating it, making it better.\nOur end goal is different, so I don't think we can be compared to them.
column6: 三人执政团为了{i}他们自己{/i}改变了这个世界，对吧？\n我们不是在干那种事。我们是在解放它，让它变得更好。\n我们的最终目标不同，所以我认为我们不能和他们相提并论。

column5: You have a point, actually. Maybe I've got the wrong idea.\nA flipped coin does the same thing until it lands, after all.\nThe truth is only shown after everything is said and done.
column6: 其实你说得有道理。也许我想错了。\n毕竟，抛起的硬币在落地之前，看起来都一样。\n直到一切尘埃落定，真相才会显现。

column5: Exactly!
column6: 正是如此！

column5: In that case, maybe I do side with Vivien.\nWith Ulric's strength, he may stand a chance.\nI hope [firstname] is on the same page as us.
column6: 既然如此，也许我确实站在薇薇安这边。\n以乌尔里克的力量，或许有一拼之力。\n希望[firstname]和我们想法一致。

column5: I guess we'll find out once we get to the ball.\nBut I wonder if Draycu will request our aid...?\nAnd for that matter, who will his Champion be?
column6: 我想等我们到了舞会就知道了。\n不过，我很好奇德雷库会不会请求我们相助……？\n还有，他的斗士会是谁？

column5: Gosh, I hope things don't get even {i}more{/i} complicated.\nI'm not sure I could handle a web more tangled than this.
column6: 天哪，希望事情别再变得更{i}复杂{/i}了。\n我不确定自己能应付比这更纠缠不清的乱局。

column5: Oh come on, what's the worst that could happen...?
column6: 哦，得了吧，还能糟到哪儿去……？

column5: Pro, what do you think you're doing!?\nI had a plan, and now you've ruined everything!
column6: 普洛，你以为你在干什么！？\n我本来有计划，现在你把一切都毁了！

column5: Sorry Ulric, it just made sense.\nThis is a fight to the death, right?\nDraycu has {i}never{/i} lost. I had to do it.
column6: 抱歉，乌尔里克，但那样做才合理。\n这是生死决斗，对吧？\n德雷库{i}从未{/i}输过。我不得不这么做。

column5: I had everything under control.
column6: 我本来把一切都控制住了。

column5: It's not your job to control everything!\nYou need to get that through your thick skull!
column6: 控制一切不是你的职责！\n你得把这一点刻进你那顽固的脑子里！

column5: You're going to regret this.
column6: 你会后悔的。

column5: Regret? I can live with that.\nIt's better than dying for nothing.\nDraycu has killed stronger men than you.
column6: 后悔？我能承受。\n总比为毫无意义的事送命强。\n德雷库杀过比你更强的人。

column5: I don't think he's going to lose this battle.\nThat's why I want to be on his good side.
column6: 我不觉得这场战斗他会输。\n所以我才想站在他那边。

column5: So you're just going to suck up to him?\nGet out of my sight, Pro. You're pitiful.
column6: 所以你就打算去巴结他？\n滚出我的视线，普洛。你真可悲。

column5: Hey, umm, Draycu?
column6: 嘿，呃，德雷库？

column5: Yes...?
column6: 什么事……？

column5: This is a really nice castle you've got here.
column6: 你这座城堡真不错。

column5: Thank you.
column6: 谢谢。

column5: I was admiring it from the outside.\nI noticed it's built in a really interesting way.\nIt's pretty bumpy. Lots of places for footholds.
column6: 我刚在外面欣赏它。\n我注意到它的构造很有意思。\n表面坑坑洼洼的。有很多可以落脚的地方。

column5: Footholds...?
column6: 落脚点……？

column5: Yeah, like places to rest your feet.\nI was actually going to ask you about that.\nWas it built that way intentionally? For climbing?
column6: 对，就是能让脚歇一歇的地方。\n我其实正想问你这件事。\n它是故意造成那样的吗？为了攀爬？

column5: Every ruler adds to this castle in their own way.\nI've been in power for several decades by now.\nYou're the only one who's ever noticed my addition.
column6: 每位统治者都会以自己的方式为这座城堡添砖加瓦。\n我掌权至今已有几十年了。\n你是唯一一个注意到我那份改动的人。

column5: You made it that way!?\nDoes that mean you like to climb, too?
column6: 那是你造的！？\n这么说你也喜欢攀爬？

column5: Yes, it does. \nThat's how I start my day.\nThere's no workout quite like it.
column6: 没错。\n我每天就是这样开始的。\n没有什么锻炼能比得上它。

column5: Do you use any special equipment?\nI got some metallic claw-like things in Mazeo.
column6: 你会用什么特别的装备吗？\n我在马泽奥弄到了一些金属爪一样的东西。

column5: I have no use for such things.\nI prefer to go it alone, without safety.\nIt makes you think about every little move.
column6: 那种东西我用不着。\n我更喜欢独自攀登，不靠保护措施。\n那样你才会对每一个细微动作都深思熟虑。

column5: One accident, and you fall to your death.\nYou don't need those claws. Just climb smarter.\nA handicap takes away your sense of achivement.
column6: 一次失手，你就会坠落身亡。\n你不需要那些爪子。只要爬得更聪明些。\n外物的辅助会剥夺你的成就感。

column5: I think I'll need them, actually.\nI'm planning to climb The Grand Tree in Valinorth.\nIf you saw it, you'd understand the necessity.
column6: 其实我想我会需要的。\n我打算去爬瓦利诺斯的那棵巨树。\n你要是见过它，就会明白这是必要的。

column5: The Grand Tree, hmm...?\nDoes it live up to its namesake?
column6: 巨树，嗯……？\n它名副其实吗？

column5: Yeah, it does!\nIt's probably the ultimate challenge.\nIt overlooks the entire world, you know.
column6: 是啊，名副其实！\n那大概是终极的挑战。\n你知道的，它能俯瞰整个世界。

column5: Interesting. Very interesting.\nPerhaps I should pay Valinorth a visit one day.\nI never thought the mainland could provide me with a challenge.
column6: 有意思。非常有意思。\n也许哪天我该去瓦利诺斯走一趟。\n我从没想过大陆能给我带来挑战。

column5: Oh, it can! Trust me.\nI've been climbing my entire life.\nWant to hear about more fun places...?
column6: 哦，它能的！相信我。\n我这一辈子都在攀爬。\n想听听更多好玩的地方吗……？

column5: I can spare some time, yeah.
column6: 我确实能挤出点时间。

column5: Wow, this place is incredible.\nDraycu sure knows how to throw a party.\nWhat about you, Ulric? Having fun?
column6: 哇，这地方太棒了。\n德雷库办起宴会来真是有一套。\n你呢，乌尔里克？玩得开心吗？

column5: Draycu is my enemy, Valessa.\nWe're practically being held prisoner.\nDespite that — yeah — I'm having a good time.
column6: 德雷库是我的敌人，瓦莱莎。\n我们简直就像被囚禁的犯人。\n尽管如此——是啊——我玩得挺开心。

column5: I could tell, actually.\nHow many drinks is that? Five?\nYou don't want to fight with a hangover, do you?
column6: 其实我看得出来。\n那是第几杯了？第五杯？\n你总不想宿醉着去战斗吧？

column5: It wouldn't be the first time.\nI've taught myself to fight in any state of being.\nJust something you learn to do when you're as old as I am.
column6: 那也不是头一回了。\n我练就了在任何状态下都能战斗的本事。\n等你到了我这把年纪，自然就学会了。

column5: And how old is that...?
column6: 那到底是多大年纪……？

column5: Old enough. Besides, I doubt I'll have much trouble tomorrow.\nEven if I fought Draycu while drunk, I could take him down.\nSo don't worry about my well being. I've got this.
column6: 足够老了。再说，我不觉得明天会有什么麻烦。\n就算喝醉了和德雷库打，我也能把他撂倒。\n所以别担心我的安危。我心里有数。

column5: You can fight while you're drunk, too...?
column6: 你喝醉了也能战斗……？

column5: Of course. It actually makes things easier.\nYour movements are sloppy, and unpredictable.\nThat's all you need to confuse and overpower your opponent.
column6: 当然。实际上那还会让事情更容易。\n你的动作会变得马虎、难以预测。\n要迷惑并压制对手，这就足够了。

column5: Wow, I never thought of it that way.\nThat's a pretty unique fighting style.\nYou'll be sober tomorrow though, right?
column6: 哇，我从没这么想过。\n这真是种独特的战斗风格。\n不过你明天会清醒的吧？

column5: Depends on how tonight goes.\nDon't worry about me, I'll be fine.\nJust go and have a good time, alright?
column6: 那得看今晚怎么过了。\n别担心我，我会没事的。\n去好好玩吧，行吗？

column5: Alright, if you say so.\nThis is gonna be super interesting.\nTwo undefeated men, locked in combat.
column6: 好吧，既然你这么说。\n这会超级有意思的。\n两个未尝败绩的男人，陷入激战。

column5: Yeah, I'll make sure to put on a good show for you.\nIt's like a sport. Everybody will be watching intently.\nYou better cheer for me. I'll be listening, Valessa.
column6: 是啊，我一定会为你们献上一场好戏。\n这就像一场竞技。所有人都会目不转睛地看。\n你最好为我加油。我会听着的，瓦莱莎。

column5: Sure...!
column6: 当然……！

column5: So, Pro, are you having a good time?
column6: 那么，普洛，你玩得开心吗？

column5: Of course. All according to plan.\nI know Ulric is mad, but he'll get over it.\nWe can win this without either of us dying.
column6: 当然。一切都在计划之中。\n我知道乌尔里克很生气，但他会消气的。\n我们可以不必让任何一方送命就赢下这场。

column5: Yeah, just take out the Leader, right?\nUlric is stubborn though, so be careful.\nI think he might actually try to kill you.
column6: 是啊，只要干掉领袖就行了，对吧？\n不过乌尔里克很固执，小心点。\n我觉得他可能真的会想杀了你。

column5: I've been watching him spar for years.\nI'll be fine — I know exactly how he operates.\nThe best weapon is knowledge, right?
column6: 我看着他练武好多年了。\n我会没事的——我太清楚他的路数了。\n最好的武器就是情报，对吧？

column5: You remembered my lessons!
column6: 你记得我教的课！

column5: How could I forget...?\nIt'll help me win this battle. I know it.\nMake sure to cheer me on, alright?
column6: 我怎么会忘……？\n它会帮我赢下这场战斗的。我确信。\n记得为我加油，好吗？

column5: I think I'd like to remain silent, actually.\nI can't be taking sides at a time like this.\nAs long as we get an alliance, I'm happy.
column6: 其实我想保持沉默。\n这种时候我不能选边站。\n只要我们能结成同盟，我就满意了。

column5: Oh come on, not even gonna clap for me?\nI'll remember that when you give another speech.
column6: 哦，得了吧，连掌都不给我鼓一下？\n等你下次演讲的时候，我会记着这事的。

column5: I think my days of giving speeches are over, Pro.\nThat honor belongs to [firstname] now. \nBut I'm sure they'd say the same as me.
column6: 我想我演讲的日子已经过去了，普洛。\n那份荣幸现在属于[firstname]。\n不过我相信他们也会说和我一样的话。

column5: Man, I hate how neutral everybody is acting.\nSometimes it's alright to take a side.
column6: 唉，我真讨厌每个人都摆出一副中立的样子。\n有时候选边站也没什么不好。

column5: Well, it's not that I'm not taking a side.\nIt's more like — I shouldn't gossip to you.\nYou're a combatant, it'd affect your morale.
column6: 这个嘛，不是我没选边。\n更像是——我不该跟你嚼舌根。\n你是参赛者，那会影响你的士气。

column5: What an interesting way to tell me that you side with Ulric.\nSometimes {i}not{/i} saying something, tells me all I need to hear.
column6: 用这种方式告诉我你站在乌尔里克那边，真有意思。\n有时候{i}不{/i}说什么，就足以让我明白一切。

column5: Now you're just putting words in my mouth.\nThe only person I'd tell is [firstname].
column6: 你这是在替我说话。\n我唯一会告诉的人就是[firstname]。

column5: Interesting.
column6: 有意思。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: You're not the first person to unconditionally trust [firstname].\nPerhaps I could use that to my advantage in the future...
column6: 你不是第一个无条件信任[firstname]的人。\n也许将来我能利用这一点……

column5: I think this is where I get back to the party.\nThis whole scheming business isn't really for me.\nBut I doubt [firstname] would abuse their role for you.
column6: 我想我该回到宴会去了。\n这种勾心斗角的事实在不适合我。\n不过我怀疑[firstname]不会为你滥用他们的职权。

column5: You're probably right, Damek.\nThey'd have to do it without knowing.\nJust imagine the swindling I could do...!
column6: 你大概说得对，达梅克。\n他们得在不知情的情况下才行。\n想象一下我能干出多少骗人的勾当……！

column5: Do we know how to throw parties, or what?
column6: 我们办起宴会来可真是有一套，对吧？

column5: Who do you mean, by \"we\"?
column6: 你说的“我们”，是指谁？

column5: Our people. Like, the pure ones.\nWe're different civilizations, remember?\nDid The Old Monarchy party like this?
column6: 我们的人民。就是那些纯血者。\n我们是不同的文明，记得吗？\n旧王室也这样办宴会吗？

column5: This line of questioning is pointless.\nWhy do you wish to know such trivial information?
column6: 这种追问毫无意义。\n你为什么想知道这种琐碎的信息？

column5: It's what friends do, Howl.\nHaven't you ever heard of hanging out...?\nYou just talk to each other, about everything.
column6: 朋友就是这样，豪尔。\n你没听说过“一起闲混”吗……？\n就是互相聊天，什么都说。

column5: Well, The Old Monarchy {i}did{/i} party.\nAnd to be honest, there isn't much difference.\nDo you see this as a sort of competition?
column6: 这个嘛，旧王室{i}确实{/i}办宴会。\n说实话，差别不大。\n你把这当成某种竞赛了吗？

column5: Not exactly. Well, maybe?\nIt's always cool to know you have the most fun.\nDo you not compare yourself to other people...?
column6: 不完全是。嗯，也许吧？\n知道自己玩得最尽兴总归挺酷的。\n你从不拿自己跟别人比较吗……？

column5: That would be a waste of time.\nThere is no benefit in being like other people.\nWe simply wish to be ourselves. Unique.
column6: 那会是浪费时间。\n和别人一样没有任何好处。\n我们只愿做我们自己。独一无二。

column5: See? This is what friends do. They just talk.\nKeep going, Howl. Tell me what's on your mind.\nYou don't need a specific topic, or anything.
column6: 看到了吗？朋友就是这样。就是聊天。\n继续说，豪尔。说说你在想什么。\n你不需要什么特定的话题之类的。

column5: We would ask why you consider us a friend.\nDoes the world benefit from this conversation?\nIs there a purpose to this sort of interaction?
column6: 我们倒要问问，你为何把我们视为朋友。\n这场对话对世界有益吗？\n这种交流有什么目的吗？

column5: Perhaps we should talk about the matter at hand.\nThere is much to discuss about Vivien and Draycu.
column6: 也许我们该谈谈眼前的事。\n关于薇薇安和德雷库，有许多要讨论的。

column5: Nope, we can't talk about that.\nThat's {i}work{/i} stuff. We're here to unwind.
column6: 不行，我们不能谈那个。\n那是{i}工作{/i}上的事。我们是来放松的。

column5: Another concept we do not understand.\nEvery moment we waste, the enemy gets stronger.
column6: 又是一个我们无法理解的概念。\n我们浪费的每一刻，敌人都变得更强大。

column5: It's not a waste, though!\nIf our bond grows stronger, then so do we.\nIt's important to get along with your comrades, Howl.
column6: 可这不是浪费！\n如果我们的羁绊加深，我们也会变强。\n和同伴好好相处很重要，豪尔。

column5: Very well. We will try.\nThis party is an interesting experience.\nAre you having a good time, Fortaime...?
column6: 很好。我们会试试。\n这场宴会是一次有趣的体验。\n你玩得开心吗，福泰姆……？

column5: There we go! Now you're doing it right.\nJust a few more steps and you'll be ready to dance.
column6: 这就对了！你现在做得很好。\n再练几步，你就能跳舞了。

column5: We would rather die.
column6: 我们宁愿去死。

column5: Hey, Valessa?
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎？

column5: Yeah? What's up?
column6: 嗯？怎么了？

column5: I saw you dancing with [firstname]...
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]跳舞了……

column5: And...?
column6: 然后呢……？

column5: Are you two a thing now?
column6: 你们俩现在在一起了？

column5: Does it matter...?
column6: 这重要吗……？

column5: No, I was just curious! Really!\nAs you know, we're already dating.\nI just figured it'd be my business, too.
column6: 不，我只是好奇！真的！\n你也知道，我们已经在交往了。\n我只是觉得这也该算我的事。

column5: Well then, I guess we are.\nIt was all so \"in the moment\".\nI guess we can work out specifics later?
column6: 那么，我想是吧。\n一切都那么“顺其自然”。\n具体的事，我们以后再说，好吗？

column5: Sounds good to me!\nThis is pretty awesome, isn't it?\nNothing can tear the three of us apart...!
column6: 我没意见！\n这真棒，不是吗？\n没什么能把我们三个分开……！

column5: Yeah, I guess you're right.\nNo matter what, we're always together.\nValinorth, Mazeo, Alarinthia, and soon enough, Balteus...
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n无论如何，我们始终在一起。\n瓦利诺斯、马泽奥、阿拉林西亚，很快还有巴尔泰乌斯……

column5: Oh yeah — the final attack...\nI just hope we all survive it, don't you?\nI'd hate to get close to you both, and then lose you.
column6: 哦对——最后的大决战……\n我只希望我们都能活着挺过去，你呢？\n我可不想和你们俩刚亲近起来，就失去你们。

column5: Well I have no intentions of dying, Fortaime.\nI'm just worried about [firstname], though. \nThe stress that this quest is bringing {i}me{/i} is unreal.
column6: 我可没打算死，福泰姆。\n不过我只是担心[firstname]。\n这趟旅程给{i}我{/i}带来的压力大得难以置信。

column5: I can't even imagine being the one in charge.\nTo rule this world after the war is over...?\nHopefully I can help make it easier.
column6: 我根本无法想象当那个掌权的人会是什么样。\n战争结束后要统治这个世界……？\n但愿我能帮忙让它轻松些。

column5: Yeah, same! That's my main goal in all of this.\nWe're all a team, so we need to help each other out.\nI'll have your back as long as you have mine, Valessa.
column6: 是啊，我也是！这就是我做这一切的主要目标。\n我们都是一个团队的，就该互相帮助。\n只要你支持我，我就会支持你，瓦莱莎。

column5: Of course, and then we can both protect [firstname].\nWe'll all be looking out for each other. Totally unstoppable.\nI can picture The Triumvirate quaking in their boots right now.
column6: 当然，然后我们就能一起保护[firstname]了。\n我们会互相照应。所向披靡。\n我都能想象三人执政团现在吓得发抖的样子。

column5: Heh, yeah. We'll take them down no problem.\nSo what do you say...? Together until the end?
column6: 嘿，是啊。我们会轻而易举地干掉他们。\n所以你说呢……？一起走到最后？

column5: Until the end.
column6: 直到最后。

column5: Well, I was just curious!\nIt seemed pretty passionate from what I saw.\nThink you're gonna rule at [firstname]'s side?
column6: 唔，我只是好奇！\n从我看到的来看，还挺深情的。\n你觉得你会和[firstname]并肩统治吗？

column5: I didn't even think of that, to be honest.\nBut we all worked together in Valinorth, right?\nNo matter what happens, I'm sure we'll make it work.
column6: 说实话，我根本没想过这个。\n但我们在瓦利诺斯时就是一起共事的，对吧？\n无论发生什么，我相信我们都能处理好。

column5: Of course, my queen.
column6: 当然，我的女王。

column5: Whoa, hold on. {i}Please{/i} don't call me that.
column6: 哇，等等。{i}拜托{/i}别这么叫我。

column5: Yes, your highness.
column6: 遵命，殿下。

column5: Fortaime...!
column6: 福泰姆……！

column5: Oh, lighten up — I'm just messing around.\nI know you'd make a fine ruler. You're awesome.
column6: 哦，放松点——我只是开个玩笑。\n我知道你会是个出色的统治者。你很棒。

column5: Really...?
column6: 真的吗……？

column5: Of course...! And it's a real possibility too.\nDating [firstname]...? Do the math, Valessa.
column6: 当然……！而且这完全有可能。\n和[firstname]交往……？自己算算吧，瓦莱莎。

column5: Hmm...
It's not {i}that{/i} complicated.\nEvery King needs a Queen, right?\nI think you fit the bill perfectly. Don't you?
column6: 没那么{i}复杂{/i}。\n每个国王都需要一位王后，对吧？\n我觉得你完全适合这个位置。你不觉得吗？

column5: Although I guess having two Queens could be complicated.\nMaybe you'd need to have a separate title, but that changes nothing.\nI still think that you fit the bill of ruler perfectly. Don't you agree with me?
column6: 虽然我想，有两个王后可能会有点复杂。\n也许你需要另一个头衔，但那改变不了什么。\n我仍然觉得你完全适合当统治者。你同意我的看法吗？

column5: I can't answer that question.\nIt would be pretty self serving, wouldn't it?
column6: 我没法回答这个问题。\n那会显得太自吹自擂了，不是吗？

column5: A Queen has no need to be humble, Valessa.\nDrink fancy tea, wear beautiful dresses — do it all!\nI just hope you don't forget about me when you're famous.
column6: 王后不需要谦逊，瓦莱莎。\n喝精致的茶，穿漂亮的裙子——全都来一遍！\n我只希望等你出名了，别忘了我。

column5: Fortaime, I'd never forget about you.\nAt the very least, you'd make sure of that...\nBut we'd definitely need a royal advisor, right?
column6: 福泰姆，我永远不会忘了你。\n至少，你会确保这一点的……\n不过我们肯定需要一位王室顾问，对吧？

column5: Are you suggesting what I think you're suggesting?
column6: 你是不是在暗示我以为你在暗示的事？

column5: Well, we all worked together back in Valinorth.\nI don't see why it would be any different after the war.\nImagine the three of us being rulers of the entire world.
column6: 这个嘛，我们在瓦利诺斯时就一起共事。\n我看不出战后会有什么不同。\n想象一下我们三个统治整个世界。

column5: Awesome!
column6: 太棒了！

column5: When we enter the library, Damek rushes forward.{w}\nHe closes a few books, and tidies the room as I catch up.
column6: 我们走进图书馆时，达梅克快步上前。{w}\n我赶上时，他合上几本书，收拾着房间。

column5: Terribly sorry about the mess!\nIt was impolite of me to leave it this way.
column6: 真抱歉，这么乱！\n把它丢成这样是我失礼了。

column5: After a few more moments, he stops cleaning up.{w}\nIt didn't really bother me. He's just trying to make a good impression.
column6: 又过了一会儿，他停止了收拾。{w}\n这其实并不困扰我。他只是想留个好印象。

column5: Well, there's not much to say about the library.\nAs the dust would show, it doesn't get much use.\nBut you'll find books here on pretty much everything.
column6: 这个嘛，关于图书馆没什么好说的。\n看这灰尘就知道，这里没什么人用。\n不过你几乎能找到关于一切的书。

column5: It's a great place to brush up on stuff you might be rusty on.\nIt has a decent collection, too. If it's out there, it's probably in here.\nFeel free to use it at your leisure. It's quite peaceful.
column6: 这是个温习你可能生疏的知识的好地方。\n藏书也相当可观。只要世上有的，这里可能都有。\n你随时可以随意使用。这里很清静。

column5: He smiles, as he makes his way back to the main landing.{w}\nThis place was pretty big. I'm surprised they have so many books.{w}\nIt's almost a shame that they don't get much use. Maybe I can change that.
column6: 他微笑着，走回主平台。{w}\n这地方挺大的。他们有这么多书让我很惊讶。{w}\n这些书没什么人用，几乎有点可惜。也许我可以改变这一点。

column5: The Rebel HQ Library contains every book you've read on your journey.{w}\nBrush up on knowledge, and check on the status of your collection.{w}\nIt's a great way to read books without revisiting older areas.
column6: 反抗军总部图书馆收录了你旅途中读过的每一本书。{w}\n温习知识，查看你的藏书状态。{w}\n这是无需重游旧地就能读书的好方法。

column5: There's a necklace on the table here.{w}\nIt feels like it's calling out to me.
column6: 这儿的桌上有一条项链。{w}\n它仿佛在向我呼唤。

column5: I walk through the main atrium of the Rebel HQ.{w}\nIt's not fully clean. Blood still stains the floor. Armor is scattered about.{w}\nI'm not sure what they planned to do with the pieces of The Honor Guard.
column6: 我穿过反抗军总部的主中庭。{w}\n这里没有完全清理干净。地板上还留有血迹。盔甲散落各处。{w}\n我不确定他们打算怎么处理荣誉卫队的残骸。

column5: Sovy is looking around, and he appears sad.{w}\nI don't blame him. This is where he launched his attack.{w}\nHim and his men killed almost all of us. We almost lost that day.
column6: 索维环顾四周，看起来很悲伤。{w}\n我不怪他。这里就是他发动进攻的地方。{w}\n他和他的手下几乎杀光了我们。那一天我们差点就输了。

column5: I already had my doubt when we launched this attack.\nIf only we had our fight a little bit earlier. I could've prevented this.\nTouching that blade at the same time as you — that was the catalyst.
column6: 我们发动这次进攻时，我就已经有疑虑了。\n要是我们的决斗再早一点就好了。我本可以阻止这一切。\n和你同时碰到那把剑——那就是导火索。

column5: I don't think you knew the truth of The Monarchy at that point.\nIt's almost as if they were calling out to me. Trying to change my stance.\nWell, I suppose it worked — I stand here, ready to repay you for my sins.
column6: 我想那时你还不知道王室的真相。\n几乎就像是他们在向我呼唤。试图改变我的立场。\n好吧，我想它奏效了——我站在这里，准备为我的罪孽向你赎罪。

column5: His words seem so genuine, it's almost hard to think he could be lying.{w}\nAt first, he seemed unsure about whether or not he'd rejoin The Triumvirate.{w}\nWhat started out as a revenge quest against Halin has certainly grown quickly.
column6: 他的话听起来如此真诚，几乎让人无法相信他会撒谎。{w}\n起初，他似乎还不确定是否要重新加入三人执政团。{w}\n一场最初针对哈林的复仇之旅，无疑已经迅速壮大了。

column5: But we mustn't waste time on talk like that.\nFocusing on the past stops you from seeing the future.\n{i}That's{/i} what is truly important. Your assault on Balteus.
column6: 但我们不能在那种空谈上浪费时间。\n沉溺于过去会让你看不见未来。\n{i}那{/i}才是真正重要的。你对巴尔泰乌斯的进攻。

column5: I agree. Sovy doesn't seem like one to waste time with pleasantries.
column6: 我同意。索维不像是会浪费时间说客套话的人。

column5: So I guess I'll be teaching you {i}two{/i} lessons this time.\nFirst of all — focus on the war. Don't waste time with being friendly.\nI've seen you and your comrades. That bond is dangerous during battle.
column6: 所以这次我想我要教你{i}两{/i}课。\n首先——专注于战争。别浪费时间讲交情。\n我见过你和你的同伴。那种羁绊在战斗中很危险。

column5: We can't have you taking a sword for a loved one.\nYou are this world's future, [firstname]. You need to be smart.\nFeelings...? They cloud judgment. I know this all too well, and so should you.
column6: 我们不能让你为了所爱之人去挨剑。\n你是这个世界的未来，[firstname]。你得聪明点。\n感情……？它们会蒙蔽判断力。这一点我太清楚了，你也该清楚。

column5: And in your situation, it is best to rely on things that serve you without hesitation.\nA friend with emotional stakes may not follow every order. That is a major flaw.\nThat blade, however — and the beings it can create — will cater to your desire.
column6: 而在你的处境下，最好依靠那些会毫不犹豫为你效力的东西。\n一个牵涉情感的友人未必会服从每一个命令。这是个大缺陷。\n而那把剑——以及它能创造出的存在——则会迎合你的意愿。

column5: He points to the suits of armor scattered around the floor.{w}\nThat means the next lesson must be related to The Honor Guard.{w}\nThe Triumvirate could create a near-infinite amount. Could I do that, too?
column6: 他指向散落一地的盔甲。{w}\n这意味着下一课一定和荣誉卫队有关。{w}\n三人执政团能创造出近乎无限的数量。我也能做到吗？

column5: Normally the blade requires a sacrifice, and the energy within, to power that armor.\nBut there is so much energy within you — I wonder if you could do it by yourself.\nImagine an entire force of Honor Guard soldiers serving you. Such power.
column6: 通常这把剑需要祭品，以及其中的能量，才能驱动那些盔甲。\n但你体内有如此充沛的能量——我在想你是否能独自做到。\n想象一整支为你效力的荣誉卫队。何等强大的力量。

column5: The Triumvirate is right to want that blade back. In your hands, it is a threat.\nAnd it makes sense why they'd want you dead, too. You are {i}The Monarchy{/i}.\nTake out that blade for me, [firstname]. Let's see if you can do what I think you can.
column6: 三人执政团想夺回那把剑是理所当然的。在你手里，它就是个威胁。\n他们想置你于死地也合情合理。你就是{i}王室{/i}。\n把剑拿出来给我看看，[firstname]。看看你能不能做到我认为你能做到的事。

column5: I do as instructed, and take out the blade.
column6: 我照吩咐做了，取出那把剑。

column5: It responds to your will, your desire.\nThink of it as an extension of your body.\nA new muscle — ready to be trained.
column6: 它回应你的意志，你的渴望。\n把它当作你身体的延伸。\n一块新的肌肉——等待被锻炼。

column5: Hold it out, toward those scattered pieces of armor.\nSee if your resolve is strong enough to give them life.\nThat's all it takes. A spark in your mind, to ignite a flame.
column6: 把它朝那些散落的盔甲举起来。\n看看你的决心是否强到足以赋予它们生命。\n要的就是这个。你心中的一点火花，去点燃一团烈焰。

column5: I hold out the blade, pointing it toward the suits of armor.{w}\nI keep my eyes focused on them, trying to control them.{w}\nThe pieces start to move, rocking back and forth.
column6: 我举起剑，指向那些盔甲。{w}\n我目不转睛地盯着它们，试图控制它们。{w}\n那些残片开始动了起来，前后摇晃。

column5: I focus with all of my strength, and they start to shake more.{w}\nBut as Sovy mentioned, it's like a new muscle. I can't flex it for long.{w}\nThe pieces stop shaking, and remain still, just as soon as they began to move.
column6: 我倾尽全力集中精神，它们抖得更厉害了。{w}\n但正如索维所说，这就像一块新肌肉。我坚持不了多久。{w}\n那些残片刚一活动起来，就停止颤抖，归于静止。

column5: Disappointing.
column6: 令人失望。

column5: I scoff at him, and assume a neutral stance.
column6: 我朝他哼了一声，摆出中立的姿态。

column5: It seems as if you can only use the blade while under duress.\nI suppose that's not too bad. We'll be in Balteus soon enough, after all.\nAt least now you know what to do. Follow my directions, and you'll be fine.
column6: 看来你只有在身处险境时才能使用那把剑。\n我想这也不算太糟。毕竟我们很快就到巴尔泰乌斯了。\n至少现在你知道该怎么做了。照我的指示来，你会没事的。

column5: He starts to walk away, but quickly turns around.
column6: 他正要走开，却很快又转过身来。

column5: There won't be enough time for you to master your fears.\nYou might have to embrace these dangerous situations in order to prevail.\nBut that blade is so powerful, I'd do whatever it takes to harness that power.
column6: 你没有足够的时间去克服恐惧。\n为了取胜，你可能不得不去拥抱这些危险的处境。\n但那把剑如此强大，为了驾驭那份力量，我会不惜一切代价。

column5: I'll see you around, [firstname].\nFeel free to keep practicing if you feel the need.\nThis is going better than I expected, to say the least.
column6: 回头见，[firstname]。\n如果你觉得有必要，随时可以继续练习。\n至少可以说，这比我预期的顺利。

column5: This time, he dismisses himself for real.
column6: 这一次，他是真的告辞了。

column5: Embrace the danger to become more powerful...?{w}\nThat seemed like backwards logic, but a lot of things were backwards lately.{w}\nIf the blade responded to my fear, and danger — then I guess I knew what to do.
column6: 拥抱危险来变得更强……？{w}\n这听起来像是颠倒的逻辑，但最近很多事都是颠倒的。{w}\n如果那把剑回应我的恐惧和危险——那我想我知道该怎么做了。

column5: Because Sovy was right. I could never retrain myself in time for our final attack.{w}\nWhat an odd situation to be in. But I guess in my position, I couldn't eschew risk.{w}\nHis implication was that — if I were in danger — the suits of armor would've risen up.
column6: 因为索维说得对。我根本来不及在最后的大决战前重新训练自己。{w}\n这处境真奇怪。但我想，以我的位置，我没法回避风险。{w}\n他言下之意是——如果我身处危险——那些盔甲就会活过来。

column5: When the time comes — I can only hope that his prediction is correct.{w}\nI wonder what other lessons there are to learn. What else could the blade do?{w}\nPerhaps I'll learn more from Sovy the next time we meet. Wherever that ended up being.
column6: 到时候——我只能希望他的预测是对的。{w}\n我不知道还有什么别的课要学。那把剑还能做什么？{w}\n也许下次见到索维时，我能学到更多。不管那会在哪里。

column5: His advice keeps playing on repeat in my mind.{w}\nEmotional stakes could be a hindrance in battle...?{w}\nWould I truly let something like that endanger our cause?
column6: 他的建议在我脑中反复回响。{w}\n情感的牵绊在战斗中会成为阻碍……？{w}\n我真会让那样的事危及我们的事业吗？

column5: Would I sacrifice myself to save a comrade...?{w}\nOr in this case — I guess it works the other way around.{w}\nI close my eyes, and pray that we never have to find out.
column6: 我会牺牲自己去救同伴吗……？{w}\n又或者，在这种情况下——我想反过来也成立。{w}\n我闭上眼，祈祷我们永远不必知道答案。

column5: We enter my personal quarters after a small trek through the HQ.{w}\nIt's larger than I thought it would be. The bed as well, is quite big.{w}\nThere isn't much of a tour to be had, so Damek sighs in relief.
column6: 在总部里走了一小段路后，我们走进了我的私人房间。{w}\n它比我预想的要大。床也相当大。{w}\n没什么可参观的，达梅克于是松了口气。

column5: Well, that about ends the tour.\nAfter this, it's just the crew quarters and the war table.\nI imagine this is where you'll spend most of your spare time.
column6: 好了，参观差不多到此结束了。\n之后只剩下船员舱和作战会议桌。\n我想你会在这里度过大部分闲暇时光。

column5: He walks to the back of the room, and inspects the shelf on the wall.{w}\nMoving books and papers aside, he seems a bit sad.
column6: 他走到房间后部，查看墙上的架子。{w}\n他把书和纸张拨到一边，显得有点伤感。

column5: This room belonged to Shane. He was dear to me.\nI sent him on a dangerous mission to The Triumvirate's castle.\nHe's been gone for a while, but I know he'll be back. I can feel it.
column6: 这个房间原本属于肖恩。他对我很重要。\n我派他去三人执政团的城堡执行一项危险任务。\n他已经离开有一阵子了，但我知道他会回来的。我能感觉到。

column5: So try not to get {i}too{/i} comfortable, alright?\nThis is just where you'll stay in the meantime.\nI wouldn't want Shane to think I forgot about him.
column6: 所以别太{i}过{/i}安顿下来，好吗？\n这只是你暂时的住处。\n我不想让肖恩以为我忘了他。

column5: I nod. That makes perfect sense.{w}\nBut I wonder why he was inspecting the shelf.{w}\nHe stopped empty-handed, so he didn't find what he wanted.
column6: 我点点头。这完全说得通。{w}\n但我不明白他为什么要查看那个架子。{w}\n他空手而止，说明没找到想要的东西。

column5: You deserve a lot of rest, at least for today.\nJust follow me for a little bit longer. We're almost done.\nI'll show you where your comrades are staying.
column6: 你该好好休息，至少今天是这样。\n再跟我走一小会儿。我们快结束了。\n我带你去看看你的同伴们住哪儿。

column5: Thanks for being so accommodating. \nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你这么周到。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Thanks for being so accommodating. \nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你这么周到。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Oh, uh — we should actually get things moving.\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 哦，呃——我们其实该加快进度了。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Oh, uh — we should actually get things moving.\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 哦，呃——我们其实该加快进度了。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Trust me, that's coming soon enough!\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 相信我，那很快就到了！\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Trust me, that's coming soon enough!\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 相信我，那很快就到了！\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Wonderful. Thank you so much.\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 太好了。非常感谢。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: Wonderful. Thank you so much.\nI'll meet you outside, [firstname].
column6: 太好了。非常感谢。\n我在外面等你，[firstname]。

column5: He walks back toward the door, and waits outside.{w}\nI guess it was time to finish this tour. Finally.{w}\nThe Crew Quarters was our next stop.
column6: 他走回门口，在外面等着。{w}\n我想是时候结束这次参观了。终于。{w}\n船员舱是我们的下一站。

column5: There's a table lined with pretty much everything I'd need.{w}\nIt seems like this room was equipped with stuff for a long stay.{w}\nHowever, something told me I wouldn't get to make much use of it.
column6: 桌上摆满了我几乎需要的一切。{w}\n看来这个房间是为一住很久而配备的。{w}\n可是，我有种感觉，我用不上多少。

column5: My training regiment would likely be intense.{w}\nEarly to rise, and late to sleep. I could tell.
column6: 我的训练计划大概会很严苛。{w}\n早起晚睡。我看得出来。

column5: Why are there candles so close to the bed?{w}\nI can understand wanting to be warm, but fire hazard much?{w}\nMaybe I'd blow them out if things got too concerning.
column6: 为什么蜡烛离床这么近？{w}\n想暖和点我能理解，但这也太有火灾隐患了吧？{w}\n要是情况太让人担心，也许我会把它们吹灭。

column5: I inspect these boxes, and they're full of food.{w}\nThey definitely stocked me up for a long stay.{w}\nThankfully it was stuff that wouldn't go bad too fast.
column6: 我查看这些箱子，里面装满了食物。{w}\n他们绝对是为长住给我囤足了粮。{w}\n幸好都是些不容易很快变质的东西。

column5: I rummage through it, impressed at the selection.{w}\nWas this all really provided by The Honor Guard?{w}\nThey don't need to eat. Just what were they doing...?
column6: 我翻找着，对这丰富的种类感到惊讶。{w}\n这些真的都是荣誉卫队提供的吗？{w}\n他们不需要进食。他们到底在做什么……？

column5: It's Shane's journal.
column6: 这是肖恩的日志。

column5: There's a bunch of scrolls and books ontop of this shelf.{w}\nThey must've belonged to the previous owner, Shane.{w}\nAs Damek mentioned, this used to be his quarters.
column6: 这个架子上放着一堆卷轴和书。{w}\n它们一定属于上一任主人，肖恩。{w}\n正如达梅克所说，这里曾是他的房间。

column5: A bit odd to give them away if he's still alive, though.{w}\nAfter investigating a bit more, I find his journal.{w}\nThe last entry is regarding his “upcoming” mission.
column6: 不过，如果他还活着，把这些东西送人有点奇怪。{w}\n再翻查一番后，我找到了他的日志。{w}\n最后一则记录是关于他“即将到来”的任务。

column5: So he was scared, but loyal to Damek.{w}\nGood thing Damek isn't the type to take advantage of that.{w}\nI'm sure Shane would carry out his goal just fine. Definitely.
column6: 所以他害怕，但对达梅克忠心耿耿。{w}\n幸好达梅克不是会利用这一点的人。{w}\n我相信肖恩会顺利完成他的目标。一定。

column5: I sat on my bed, thinking about the blade, and what I could do with it.{w}\nAs if on some sort of cue, I hear a knock on my door. Sovy enters.{w}\nHe seems much more relaxed than normal. Like he's comfortable.
column6: 我坐在床上，想着那把剑，以及我能用它做什么。{w}\n仿佛得到了某种暗示，我听到敲门声。索维走了进来。{w}\n他看起来比平时放松得多。像是很自在。

column5: So, did you manage to get any more practice in?\nOr were you just going to improvise when we got to Balteus?\nBoth are good options, given the circumstances. I'm just curious.
column6: 那么，你有没有再多练练？\n还是打算到了巴尔泰乌斯就临场发挥？\n就目前的情况看，两种都行。我只是好奇。

column5: That's good. The more the better, that's what I say.\nBut at the same time, you're limited. I trained my entire life.\nIf you only have a few days, don't expect anything substantial.
column6: 那很好。要我说，越多越好。\n但与此同时，你的时间是有限的。我可是练了一辈子。\n如果你只有几天，就别指望有什么实质性的成果。

column5: It's alright. It's not like it would matter too much, anyway.\nI've had lifetimes to train — you only got the blade a few days ago.\nDon't expect any substantial results. It's better to be more realistic.
column6: 没关系。反正也不会有太大影响。\n我有过好几辈子的时间来训练——你几天前才得到那把剑。\n别指望有什么实质性的成果。还是现实一点好。

column5: He takes a few steps forward and sits beside me on the bed.
column6: 他向前走了几步，在床边坐下。

column5: Being down here has made my mind race almost nonstop. \nI mean — what I did to you and your family is unforgivable.\nYet here we are, trying to move past it. Letting me atone.
column6: 待在下面这里，让我的思绪几乎一刻不停地翻腾。\n我是说——我对你和你家人做的事不可饶恕。\n可我们却在这里，试着放下它。让我赎罪。

column5: The most important thing on my mind, is \"why\"...?\nWhy did you welcome me with open arms after what I did?\nI feel like anybody with common sense would've put me to the blade.
column6: 我心中最重要的问题，就是“为什么”……？\n在我做了那些事之后，你为什么还张开双臂欢迎我？\n我觉得任何有点常识的人都会把我处死。

column5: I'm assuming you were the only one.\nThe look I got from your comrades was definitely condemning.\nBut then what makes you different? Why could {i}you{/i} tell...?
column6: 我猜你是唯一一个这样的人。\n你的同伴们看我的眼神绝对是充满谴责的。\n可那你又有什么不同？为什么{i}你{/i}能看得出来……？

column5: Well I guess it worked. I mean, look where we are.\nIf Ulric can redeem himself, then surely I can as well.\nHe did far worse things than I. But look at him now.
column6: 好吧，我想它奏效了。我是说，看看我们现在。\n如果乌尔里克能自我救赎，那我当然也能。\n他做过的事比我恶劣得多。可看看他现在的样子。

column5: You could've fooled me, [firstname].\nI've seen nothing but a capable ruler in you.\nIt's an honor to serve. This world is in good hands.
column6: 你可骗过我了，[firstname]。\n我在你身上只看到一个有能力的统治者。\n能为你效力是我的荣幸。这个世界交到了可靠的人手里。

column5: I assume that most people will find themselves lost at one point in their life.\nThe scary part is — that if it hasn't happened yet — it could come at any time.\nI was so foolish, thinking that anybody back in Balteus could give me direction.
column6: 我猜大多数人一生中都会有迷茫的时候。\n可怕的是——如果它还没发生——它随时都可能来临。\n我太愚蠢了，以为巴尔泰乌斯的任何人都能给我指引方向。

column5: Maybe. But mistakes are usually clear — like choosing the wrong side.\nThe fact that you have doubts? I would take that as a good sign, [firstname].\nWorry isn't always a bad thing. It can help guide you when you're lost.
column6: 也许吧。但错误通常都很明显——比如站错队。\n你会有疑虑？我倒觉得这是个好迹象，[firstname]。\n忧虑并不总是坏事。它能帮你在迷茫时找到方向。

column5: It's crazy how far that instinct has taken you.\nI did the same, even though it meant insubordination.\nIt's like — I knew I was right — no matter what happened to me.
column6: 这种直觉带你走到了这一步，真不可思议。\n我也一样，哪怕那意味着抗命。\n就像——我知道我是对的——无论我会遭遇什么。

column5: He sighs, and slumps down a little bit.
column6: 他叹了口气，微微垂下身子。

column5: Well, that's all I really wanted to talk about.\nIf you'll excuse me — I'll be on my way.\nGood luck with everything, [firstname].
column6: 好了，我想谈的就是这些。\n请恕我失陪——我该走了。\n祝你一切顺利，[firstname]。

column5: He gets up and starts to walk away, but I stop him.{w}\nThis would be a good time to get him the gift I bought.{w}\nI grab the writing utensils, and hand them over to Sovy.
column6: 他起身要走，但我叫住了他。{w}\n现在正是把我买的礼物送给他的好时机。{w}\n我拿起书写用具，交给索维。

column5: You got me a gift...?\nReally, you shouldn't have.
column6: 你给我买了礼物……？\n真的，你不用这么客气。

column5: He inspects them, with a soft smile on his face.
column6: 他端详着它们，脸上带着温柔的笑容。

column5: I was looking at these in the Town Square.\nIt means a lot to me that you did this, [firstname].\nAnybody else would've just went on with their day.
column6: 我在城镇广场上就在看这些。\n你这么做对我意义重大，[firstname]。\n换作别人，只会自顾自地继续过日子。

column5: Maybe. But I'm not just \"anybody else\".
column6: 也许吧。但我可不是什么“别人”。

column5: I don't really know what to say.\nSo I guess I'll take that as a sign to stop talking.\nThank you for thinking of me as a friend. Truly.
column6: 我真不知道该说什么。\n所以我想，这大概是个该闭嘴的信号。\n谢谢你把我当朋友。真心感谢。

column5: That's more than I can say about everybody else I know.\nIn fact — I don't think I've ever gotten a gift before — from anybody.\nNot even my Father, who these pens reminded me of in the first place.
column6: 我认识的其他人都没让我这么说过。\n事实上——我想我从前从没收到过礼物——从任何人那里。\n连我父亲都没有，而这些笔最先让我想起的正是他。

column5: He scoffs, and looks down at them once more.
column6: 他嗤笑一声，又低头看了看它们。

column5: But that's a story for another time.\nI'm here to help you, not bore you with sad tales.\nPerhaps we can talk more before we set sail.
column6: 但那故事改天再讲吧。\n我是来帮你的，不是拿悲伤的故事来烦你的。\n也许启航前我们能再聊聊。

column5: Without another word, he leaves my room for good.{w}\nI'm not sure if the choice of present was a good or bad thing, now.{w}\nIt seems to remind him of something he deemed a \"sad tale\".
column6: 他没再多说一句，就此离开了我的房间。{w}\n现在我不确定选这份礼物到底是好是坏。{w}\n它似乎让他想起了他称之为“悲伤故事”的某件事。

column5: Well, there's nothing I can do about it right now.{w}\nMaybe he'd tell me that tale the next time we spoke.{w}\nWith our final battle looming, I might not have much time.
column6: 算了，眼下我也无能为力。{w}\n也许下次交谈时他会把那故事讲给我听。{w}\n最后的大决战迫在眉睫，我可能没多少时间了。

column5: But there's one thing I can say for sure. Sovy is becoming a friend.{w}\nA second chance is a truly great thing, as long as the person is genuine.{w}\nI can tell that if I earned his loyalty, he'd be indispensable during our attack.
column6: 但有一件事我可以肯定。索维正在成为一个朋友。{w}\n只要那人是真诚的，第二次机会就是件了不起的事。{w}\n我看得出，如果我能赢得他的忠诚，他在我们的进攻中将不可或缺。

column5: He gets up and walks away, a weight clearly on his shoulders.{w}\nI'm glad I could help him out by offering answers to his questions.{w}\nBut was it enough...? Hopefully he wouldn't turn on us in Balteus.
column6: 他起身走开，肩上显然压着沉重的负担。{w}\n我很高兴能通过回答他的问题帮到他。{w}\n但这样够吗……？希望他别在巴尔泰乌斯背叛我们。

column5: Something tells me we're very close to earning his full loyalty, however.{w}\nWho once appeared to be a murderous villain, was now showing a different side.{w}\nI know that if we really did win him over — he'd be an indispensable asset in Balteus.
column6: 可我有种感觉，我们离赢得他全部的忠诚已经很近了。{w}\n曾经看似凶残恶棍的人，如今露出了不同的一面。{w}\n我知道如果我们真能把他争取过来——他在巴尔泰乌斯将是无价之宝。

column5: And if that went well, he could even become a trusted soldier.{w}\nPerhaps we'd be able to spend more time together before the final attack.{w}\nI felt like we were incredibly close to ensuring he remained on our side no matter what.
column6: 如果进展顺利，他甚至可能成为一名值得信赖的士兵。{w}\n也许在最后的大决战前，我们能多相处些时间。{w}\n我感觉我们已非常接近确保他无论如何都站在我们这边。

column5: Sovy's loyalty scene has been unlocked and awaits at the war table.
column6: 索维的忠诚剧情已解锁，在作战会议桌处等待。

column5: After exiting my room, he takes me to a large hallway.{w}\nAt the end of it is a grand door, surely leading somewhere important.{w}\nLining the sides, are smaller doors. I assume they lead to more private rooms.
column6: 走出我的房间后，他带我来到一条宽阔的走廊。{w}\n走廊尽头是一扇宏伟的门，想必通向某个重要的地方。{w}\n两侧排列着较小的门。我猜它们通向更多私人房间。

column5: That door right there leads to the war table.\nThat's the end of this tour. It's where things start.\nI'll go over our battle plan, and give you an itinerary.
column6: 那边那扇门通向作战会议桌。\n参观到此结束。那才是事情开始的地方。\n我会把作战计划和你过一遍，再给你一份行程安排。

column5: Your training will commence tomorrow.\nI can't believe this is finally happening. \nIt almost feels like a dream, you know?
column6: 你的训练明天开始。\n真不敢相信这终于要开始了。\n你知道，这几乎像一场梦。

column5: He lets out a nervous laugh, before turning to face the large door.
column6: 他紧张地笑了笑，然后转身面向那扇大门。

column5: Well, these doors on the side lead to your comrade's rooms.\nValessa and Fortaime have been given personal rooms, just like you.\nMy quarters are here as well, if you'd like to come spend time with me.
column6: 这个嘛，侧边的这些门通向你的同伴们的房间。\n瓦莱莎和福泰姆和你一样，都分到了各自的房间。\n我的房间也在这里，如果你想来找我待一会儿的话。

column5: I'm going to make a quick stop in my room, actually.\nAfter that, I'll meet you at the War Table, alright?\nTake some time to unwind, you really deserve it.
column6: 其实，我要先回房间一下。\n之后我们在作战会议桌见，好吗？\n花点时间放松一下，你真的很该歇歇了。

column5: It's been a pleasure, [firstname].
column6: 幸会，[firstname]。

column5: It's been a pleasure, [firstname].
column6: 幸会，[firstname]。

column5: With a smile, he walks off to one of the side rooms.{w}\nI guess that's the one I'd go to if I wanted to see him.{w}\nWith some long awaited free time, it might be a good idea.
column6: 他微笑着走进其中一间侧房。{w}\n我想，如果我想见他，就该去那一间。{w}\n有了期盼已久的空闲时间，去看看也许是个好主意。

column5: However, I should make sure to spend it wisely.{w}\nAs soon as I met him at the war table, things would begin.{w}\nAnd something told me that nothing would be easy moving forward.
column6: 不过，我得确保好好利用这段时间。{w}\n我一旦在作战会议桌与他碰面，一切就会开始。{w}\n而我有种感觉，往后的一切都不会轻松。

column5: I enter Fortaime's room and see him sitting at the table.{w}\nHe's engrossed in a book — it almost looks like he's studying.{w}\nI take a few steps forward and announce my presence to him.
column6: 我走进福泰姆的房间，看到他坐在桌旁。{w}\n他正埋头读一本书——看起来几乎像是在钻研。{w}\n我上前几步，向他示意我来了。

column5: Oh, hey there!\nYou might want to read this, [firstname].\nI was just looking up how to save Valinorth.
column6: 哦，你好！\n你也许想读读这个，[firstname]。\n我刚才在查怎么拯救瓦利诺斯。

column5: Oh, hey there!\nYou might want to read this, [firstname].\nI was just looking up how to save Valinorth.
column6: 哦，你好！\n你也许想读读这个，[firstname]。\n我刚才在查怎么拯救瓦利诺斯。

column5: That's right. He wants to reconnect Valinorth to the Spirit Realm.{w}\nWithout the power from their idol, Valinorth would freeze over.{w}\nAt least, that's what we thought. His next words surprised me.
column6: 没错。他想让瓦利诺斯重新与灵界相连。{w}\n没有来自他们灵像的力量，瓦利诺斯就会冻结。{w}\n至少我们一直这么以为。他接下来的话让我吃了一惊。

column5: Current scholars are losing faith in the spirit realm.\nThey call our reliance on the Spirit Idols a \"superstition\".\nWithout them, they say the world would be exactly the same.
column6: 如今的学者们正逐渐对灵界失去信心。\n他们把我们对灵像的依赖称为“迷信”。\n他们说，没有灵像，世界也会完全一样。

column5: I disregarded it at first, but then I thought about it.\nValinorth's idol has been dim for over twenty years, now.\nHave you noticed it get colder at all...? I sure haven't.
column6: 我起初没当回事，但后来想了想。\n瓦利诺斯的灵像已经黯淡二十多年了。\n你注意到天气有变冷吗……？我可没觉得。

column5: But one conclusion just brings up a million more mysteries.\nIf they aren't giving energy to the land, what are they doing...?\nIs there some purpose to the Spirit Realm that we don't know?
column6: 但一个结论只会引出无数更多的谜团。\n如果它们没有向大地输送能量，那它们在做什么……？\n灵界是不是还有什么我们不知道的目的？

column5: I mean, I like this hypothesis, I truly do.\nForgive my \"blasphemy\", but just hear me out.\nIf the idol isn't important, then Valinorth is fine.
column6: 我是说，我喜欢这个假说，真的。\n原谅我的“亵渎”，但请听我把话说完。\n如果灵像并不重要，那瓦利诺斯就没事。

column5: That means we don't need to worry about it freezing over.\nIt just brings about a new question. What {i}are{/i} the idols?\nWe know that they create Seers, but what about the idol here?
column6: 那意味着我们不必担心它会冻结。\n只是又引出一个新问题。灵像{i}究竟{/i}是什么？\n我们知道它们能造出先知，但这里那座灵像呢？

column5: And what about the idol in Alarinthia that The Triumvirate destroyed?\nThey expect us to believe that Alarinthia was always meant to be a desert?\nI was told that the destruction of their idol caused it to become lifeless.
column6: 那被三人执政团毁掉的阿拉林西亚的灵像又怎么说？\n他们想让我们相信阿拉林西亚本来就该是片沙漠吗？\n我听说正是他们灵像被毁，才使它变得毫无生机。

column5: Either way, more studying is required.\nBut I'm starting to think outside the box. I like that.\nIt's almost like Valinorth was guiding our thoughts, you know?
column6: 不管怎样，还需要更多研究。\n但我开始跳出固有思维了。我喜欢这样。\n你知道，这几乎像是瓦利诺斯在引导我们的思绪。

column5: Go against the spirits, and you're seen as evil, or crazy.\nBut out here, that's normal. It allows people to get more creative.\nI've seen a bunch of new theories about our world, and the spirits.
column6: 一旦违背灵，你就会被视为邪恶，或者疯子。\n但在这外面，那很正常。这让人能更有创造力。\n我看到了许多关于我们世界和灵的新理论。

column5: I enter Fortaime's room and see him sitting at the table.{w}\nHe's engrossed in a book — it almost looks like he's studying.{w}\nI take a few steps forward and announce my presence to him.
column6: 我走进福泰姆的房间，看到他坐在桌旁。{w}\n他正埋头读一本书——看起来几乎像是在钻研。{w}\n我上前几步，向他示意我来了。

column5: Oh, hey there! I was just studying. \nValessa gave me lots of notes about being a Scribe.\nNot that I don't know all of it. It's just nice to brush up.
column6: 哦，你好！我刚才在钻研。\n瓦莱莎给了我很多关于当书记官的笔记。\n倒不是说我不懂这些。只是温习一下挺好。

column5: Though I'm worried that sword will put me out of business.\nVisions while you're awake...? You'll always know they're visions.\nKinda puts my ability to tip you off in the garbage, doesn't it?
column6: 不过我担心那把剑会让我失业。\n清醒时就能看到预视……？你总能知道那是预视。\n那我提醒你的本事岂不是没用了？

column5: But you won't have that sword forever. Until then, I study.\nHonestly, I can't wait for things to get back to normal.\nI miss my house, and all the little things like that.
column6: 但你不会永远拥有那把剑。在那之前，我就钻研。\n说实话，我迫不及待想让一切恢复正常。\n我想念我的房子，还有那些诸如此类的小事。

column5: You take them for granted, and then they're gone.\nI just hope Valessa finds a way to save Valinorth.\nShe seems to be taking this Elder business seriously.
column6: 你不把它们当回事，然后它们就消失了。\n我只希望瓦莱莎能找到拯救瓦利诺斯的办法。\n她似乎把长老这档事看得很认真。

column5: But I wouldn't have it any other way.\nThe Elder needs to be serious, all the time.\nBeing in charge of a nation — that's incredible.
column6: 但我也不希望是别的样子。\n长老就该时时刻刻都认真。\n掌管一个国家——太了不起了。

column5: She might just be our youngest Elder, ever.\nI think that's pretty cool. We're all making history.\nI'm the first Scribe to ever operate outside Valinorth.
column6: 她说不定是我们史上最年轻的长老。\n我觉得这挺酷的。我们都在创造历史。\n我是第一个在瓦利诺斯之外活动的书记官。

column5: Anyway...
column6: 总之……

column5: He smiles, and stands up from the table.{w}\nIt looks like he's been keeping himself busy.
column6: 他笑了笑，从桌边站起身。{w}\n看来他一直让自己挺忙的。

column5: We have something {i}important{/i} to talk about...!\nI spoke to Pro, and he gave me some spending money.\nSo next time I get the chance, I'm buying that climbing gear!
column6: 我们有件{i}重要{/i}的事要谈……！\n我跟普洛说了，他给了我一些零花钱。\n所以下次有机会，我就要买那套攀爬装备！

column5: And I expect {i}you{/i} to become my Apprentice, [firstname]!\nI'll show you the ropes, and then we'll climb The Grand Tree.\nHopefully we have time for one last trip before the final battle.
column6: 而且我期待{i}你{/i}成为我的学徒，[firstname]！\n我会教你诀窍，然后我们一起去爬巨树。\n希望在最后的大决战前，我们还有时间做最后一次远行。

column5: And I expect {i}you{/i} to become my Apprentice, [firstname]!\nI'll show you the ropes, and then we'll climb The Grand Tree.\nHopefully we have time for one last trip before the final battle.
column6: 而且我期待{i}你{/i}成为我的学徒，[firstname]！\n我会教你诀窍，然后我们一起去爬巨树。\n希望在最后的大决战前，我们还有时间做最后一次远行。

column5: He runs up to me and gives me a tight hug.
column6: 他跑过来紧紧抱住我。

column5: It might be a good idea for another date, too.\nA bit more private than Mazeo's town square.\nIf we can make it to the top, that is. I sure hope so.
column6: 也许还可以再约一次会。\n比马泽奥的城镇广场更私密些。\n前提是能爬到顶。我真希望如此。

column5: He crosses his arms and gives me a sly smirk.
column6: 他双臂交叉，朝我狡黠地一笑。

column5: If you get good enough, then we can get competitive.\nIt'd be nice to have a rival. Gives me the drive to improve.\nI need that extra \"push\" if I'm gonna make it to the top.
column6: 如果你练得够好，我们就能一较高下。\n有个对手挺好的。能给我进步的动力。\n要想登顶，我就需要那股额外的“推力”。

column5: I just haven't had much time to practice my climbing.\nI hope I'm not rusty when the time comes. That'd suck.\nClimbing The Grand Tree has always been my life's goal.
column6: 我最近实在没什么时间练习攀爬。\n希望到时候别生疏了。那可就糟了。\n攀登巨树一直是我人生的目标。

column5: The first time I attempt it, I want to make sure I succeed.\nAnd they say the best way to learn, is to teach somebody else.\nSo you better prepare for some rigorous training! We're doing this.
column6: 第一次尝试，我就想确保成功。\n人们说最好的学习方式，就是去教别人。\n所以你最好做好接受严格训练的准备！我们要动真格的了。

column5: It seems like he's not about to take no for an answer.
column6: 看样子他不打算接受“不”这个答案。

column5: Oh, sorry. My mind is all over the place.\nThanks for coming to visit me, [firstname].\nIt means a lot. It really does.
column6: 哦，抱歉。我脑子乱糟糟的。\n谢谢你来看我，[firstname]。\n这对我意义重大。真的。

column5: Oh, sorry. My mind is all over the place.\nThanks for coming to visit me, [firstname].\nIt means a lot. It really does.
column6: 哦，抱歉。我脑子乱糟糟的。\n谢谢你来看我，[firstname]。\n这对我意义重大。真的。

column5: I guess you better head back to Damek.\nIsn't he waiting for you in the war room or something?\nAt least, that's what I heard. He sure loves to work.
column6: 我想你该回达梅克那儿了。\n他不是在作战室等你什么的吗？\n至少我听说是这样。他可真是热爱工作。

column5: He smiles, and then takes steps back toward the table.{w}\nBut before he gets there, he stops in his tracks, and turns around.{w}\nHe really was scatter-brained today, wasn't he? Is everything okay?
column6: 他笑了笑，然后迈步走回桌边。{w}\n但还没走到，他就停下脚步，转过身来。{w}\n他今天真是心不在焉，不是吗？一切都还好吗？

column5: There's one more thing I wanted to ask you.\nI just forgot — or, maybe I was too embarrassed.\nRemember what Damek said about the Honor Guard?
column6: 还有一件事我想问你。\n我刚才忘了——或者，也许是我太难为情了。\n记得达梅克说过的关于荣誉卫队的事吗？

column5: They're powered by the spirits of occupation victims...\nI know Valessa was thinking the same thing, about our parents.\nDo you think they're still alive? Down here, trapped in that armor?
column6: 它们是由占领受害者的灵驱动的……\n我知道瓦莱莎也在想同样的事，关于我们的父母。\n你觉得他们还活着吗？就在这下面，被困在那盔甲里？

column5: Good. I'm glad we're all on the same page.\nIt's something we can talk about more as a group.\nValessa feels the same way, she just wouldn't speak up.
column6: 很好。我很高兴我们想法一致。\n这事我们可以作为团队再深入讨论。\n瓦莱莎也是同样的感受，只是她不肯开口。

column5: I saw it in her face — back in the tunnels.\nI don't know how we'll free them, though.\nBut I think it has to do with your sword.
column6: 我在她脸上看出来了——就在那些隧道里。\n不过我不知道我们要怎么解救他们。\n但我觉得这和你的剑有关。

column5: So, until next time then?\nI'll get back to my reading.
column6: 那么，那就下次见？\n我继续看书了。

column5: Understandable. You're on the fence.\nIt's something we can talk about more as a group.\nValessa believes they're trapped in there. I know it.
column6: 可以理解。你还在犹豫。\n这事我们可以作为团队再深入讨论。\n瓦莱莎相信他们被困在里面。我知道的。

column5: I saw it in her face — back in the tunnels.\nAnd to be honest, I feel the same way as her.\nWe can free them; I just have no idea how.
column6: 我在她脸上看出来了——就在那些隧道里。\n说实话，我和她有同样的感受。\n我们能解救他们；只是我完全不知道该怎么救。

column5: Maybe it has to do with that sword of yours...?\nI should probably get back to my studies, though.\nEither way, I guess we'll find out soon enough.
column6: 也许这和你的那把剑有关……？\n不过我大概该回去钻研了。\n不管怎样，我想我们很快就会有答案。

column5: Oh, I see...\nI hope you don't judge me and Valessa then.\nWe're pretty sure that our parents are in there.
column6: 哦，我明白了……\n那希望你别因此评判我和瓦莱莎。\n我们相当确定我们的父母就在里面。

column5: We just have to figure out how we can free them.\nHonestly, I feel like it'll have to do with your sword.\nSo regardless of your beliefs, I hope you'll help us.
column6: 我们只是得弄清楚怎样才能解救他们。\n说实话，我感觉这一定和你的剑有关。\n所以不管你怎么想，我希望你能帮我们。

column5: I should probably get back to my studies, though.\nThere's lots to read, and little time to read it.\nGood luck with Damek in the war room!
column6: 不过我大概该回去钻研了。\n要读的东西很多，能读的时间却很少。\n祝你在作战室和达梅克一切顺利！

column5: He runs up to me and gives me a kiss on the cheek.{w}\nAfter that, we embrace each other and smile.
column6: 他跑过来，在我脸颊上亲了一下。{w}\n之后，我们相拥而笑。

column5: I can't wait to see you again.
column6: 我迫不及待想再见到你。

column5: He gives me a quick smile before returning to his books.{w}\nIt's admirable how much he's studying, given the circumstances.{w}\nI decide to leave him be for now, and go about my business.
column6: 他朝我匆匆一笑，便又回到书堆里。{w}\n在这种情况下他还这么用功钻研，真令人钦佩。{w}\n我决定暂时不打扰他，去忙我的事。

column5: I enter Valessa's room, and see her pacing around.{w}\nShe looks like she's in deep thought, so I clear my throat.{w}\nIt was enough to get her attention, and she turns to me with a smile.
column6: 我走进瓦莱莎的房间，看到她来回踱步。{w}\n她看起来陷入了沉思，于是我清了清嗓子。{w}\n这足以引起她的注意，她转向我，露出微笑。

column5: Oh, hey [firstname].\nI was just thinking about stuff.\nSo much has happened since we got here.
column6: 哦，嘿，[firstname]。\n我刚才在想事情。\n我们到这里之后发生了太多事。

column5: Oh, hey [firstname].\nI was just thinking about stuff.\nSo much has happened since we got here.
column6: 哦，嘿，[firstname]。\n我刚才在想事情。\n我们到这里之后发生了太多事。

column5: I'm still trying to find a way to save Valinorth.\nI found a few books, but nothing too promising.\nIn fact, some scholars doubt that the idol even helps.
column6: 我还在想办法拯救瓦利诺斯。\n我找到几本书，但都没什么希望。\n事实上，有些学者怀疑那灵像根本没用。

column5: They say it's just a superstition, or something.\nBut how else do you explain Eastcrown...?\nSuch a harsh and sudden climate change.
column6: 他们说那不过是迷信之类的。\n可东冠的事你要怎么解释……？\n如此剧烈而突然的气候变化。

column5: And how would you explain Alarinthia, for that matter?\nWas it destined to always be an arid wasteland...?\nThe spirits {i}must{/i} have something to do with it.
column6: 那阿拉林西亚又该怎么解释？\n它注定永远是一片干旱的荒地吗……？\n灵{i}一定{/i}和这有关。

column5: But there's a part of me that hopes they're right.\nIf the spirits weren't keeping us warm? Then we're fine.\nNothing bad will happen to Valinorth at all, right...?
column6: 但我心里有一部分希望他们是对的。\n如果灵并没有在为我们保暖？那我们就没事。\n瓦利诺斯根本不会出什么事，对吧……？
